newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: ANZ says Wallis approach sensible.
newsitem.headline: ANZ says Wallis approach sensible.

text.p: Australia and New Zealand Banking Group Ltd said on Wednesday the Wallis recommendations were a sensible and comprehensive approach to maintaining the stability and efficiency of Australia's financial system.

"On the face of it the recommendations, if adopted, will help improve the financial system, provide sensible streamlining of regulatory functions and increase competition," ANZ chief executive Don Mercer said in a statement.
Mercer said the majority of recommendations in the report echoed the views in ANZ's submission to the inquiry.
The Wallis inquiry recommended that the "six pillars" policy, which prevented mergers among the four biggest banks and two largest life companies, should be removed.
Treasurer Peter Costello said the government had decided to end the "six pillars" policy, but ruled out mergers between the big four banks at present.
This would be reviewed when the government was satisfied that competition, particularly in small business lending, had increased sufficiently to allow such mergers to be considered, he said.
Shares in ANZ, long viewed as a potential takeover target should the rules be relaxed, slipped 11 cents to close at A$7.89.
